slices.name: ws01-30-heritage-fonts
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 30 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD abe7d07 (the harness commit, which sits after slice 29's own commit); the base for diffs is abe7d07. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. A harness change lands on the branch as a commit of its own between slice 29 and this slice: it gives each browser-test server its own database in test/a11y/global-setup.ts, makes the baseline sampler (test/a11y/baseline.ts) and the hero-ring test (test/a11y/tokens.spec.ts) wait for their page's data, and makes the arrow-key test in test/a11y/components-edges.spec.ts press until the top. So line numbers in test/a11y/global-setup.ts, baseline.ts, tokens.spec.ts and components-edges.spec.ts, wherever this brief or the earlier records cite them, may have shifted: re-read those four files and do not trust a cited line. Every other line number below was measured on the working tree that held slice 29 finished and not yet committed, the tree this slice starts from; the harness commit is not expected to change any other file, but read any file before you edit it. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, lines 7 to 11; the acceptance table with its AC11 row (line 35), AC12 row (line 36) and AC13 row (line 37), all still Planned and all owned by step 31, so this slice has no row of its own: it adds a Step 30 sentence to the AC11 and AC12 rows and leaves AC13 alone (difference 8); the AC10 row (line 34), AC4 row (line 28) and AC7 row (line 31) as the pattern for a filled row, the AC12 row's own sentence 'Step 22 lays the first half:' as the pattern for a sentence added to a row that stays Planned, and the AC8 row (line 32), which this slice leaves alone unless the fixture page's boxes change, which they should not; the step 29 block (lines 804 to 835) and the step 28 block (lines 772 to 802) as the pattern for a step block, and the step 22 block (lines 560 to 574, with its Fonts line 571, ThemeScope line 568 and Nesting line 569) for what the scope and live.css already do; Decisions (heading at line 837): the one planned line for this step, 'Small caps (step 30)', line 1045, which this slice keeps word for word and marks done, with the three step 29 planned lines at 1042 to 1044 as the pattern for a planned line marked done; Heritage fonts (brief 0.2), line 938; JetBrains Mono is not added (step 22), line 897, and Fonts (step 21), line 555, which settle Geist Mono as the only mono face and Instrument Serif 400 as the base look's accent face (font-accent); The scope switches need newLook (step 21), line 893; One scope mechanism (step 22), line 896; Deviations (heading at line 926: the Step 29 entry, lines 1208 to 1216, as the pattern, with its sub-bullet 'Files beyond the step's list:'; the Step 22 entry from line 1130, whose line 1193 says the heritage faces' glyphs could not be checked until step 30); Verify items (heading at line 1218: the step 29 ones, lines 1432 to 1449, as the pattern; Live fonts (step 22), line 1325; Marker glyph coverage (step 27), line 1395, whose sentence 'Libre Caslon Display and Source Serif 4 are not installed' test/unit/redesign-status-step27.test.ts reads, so that line is left exactly as it is); Follow-ups (heading at line 1451: The heritage faces' glyphs (step 27), line 1600, which names this step and which this slice closes with Done in step 30; AC11 and AC12 second halves (step 22), line 1554, which gains a Step 30 sentence and is not closed; Base inside heritage in a browser (step 22), line 1552; Binding the live fonts (step 22), line 1553; Heritage on a muted panel (step 24), line 1574; The About logo in the heritage layout (step 28), line 1609, which mentions the 2-pixel radius on mats; Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS (step 23), line 1558; The a11y servers share one database (step 23), line 1564, and The baseline sampler waits for content (step 27), line 1601, which the harness commit answers and which you leave alone; K reviews the step 29 judgement calls, line 1614, as the pattern for a K-reviews follow-up), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (section 2.4 budgets, line 250; the heritage tokens, line 288, with the 2px radius sentence; Typography, lines 290 to 297, above all line 295: the faces, 'Budget ≤ 110 KB woff2, latin subset', the Georgia fallback with size-adjust and ascent-override, and the uppercase fallback at 0.85em when the subset lacks smcp and c2sc, and line 297: scope fonts load through a lazily imported CSS module; the files list, line 342, which names src/styles/themes/heritage.css and a .small-caps utility; acceptance criteria 11 and 12, lines 358 and 359; the WS01 deviations list, line 112, which ends with the step 29 sentence), docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md (lines 102 to 109, what the heritage look changes and never changes, with the small caps and Caslon rules at line 106 and the reader at line 107; lines 111 to 120, Fonts, with the budget at line 119 ('If it is over, drop the italic file first') and the Georgia fallback at line 120; line 127, ThemeScope imports src/styles/themes/<scope>.css once), src/styles/themes/live.css (21 lines: a header comment and seven @import lines, no rule; the pattern for a scope's font CSS), src/components/ThemeScope.tsx (82 lines: the header comment, lines 1 to 28, which says at line 21 that heritage's fonts arrive with the heritage pages; SCOPE_FONTS at lines 36 to 38, holding live only; loadScopeFonts at lines 42 to 49; the effect that calls it at lines 67 to 69), src/lib/themeScopes.ts (HERITAGE_ROUTES at line 43, routeScope at line 86; not changed by this slice), src/index.css (the imports, lines 1 to 9; --font-sans and --font-accent in @theme inline, lines 43 and 47; --font-mono-face at lines 250 and 416; the heritage colour block, lines 599 to 615, and its dark block, lines 617 to 630, which hold colours only; the base layer, lines 821 to 836), src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx (the only place ThemeScope renders; the heritage fixture is /__fixtures/heritage in the browser-test builds only; its h1 is text-3xl at line 87 and its h2s are text-xl), src/components/ui/card.tsx and src/components/ui/table.tsx (neither carries a data-slot), src/components/PageHero.tsx (its h1 at lines 95 and 99, text-3xl and sm:text-4xl), package.json (the font packages, lines 39 to 43) and package-lock.json (root lines 11 to 15, entries from line 2181), and the tests that pin fonts and scopes today: test/unit/tokens.test.ts (lines 802 to 817: the exact list of @import lines in src/index.css, the two exact pins, and --font-accent; lines 819 to 833: Geist Mono is named only in the new look's --font-mono-face rule, and no file under src other than index.css, CSS included and comments included, may name Geist Mono, JetBrains, Courier New, Menlo, ui-monospace or a font-[...mono] class), test/unit/token-utilities.test.ts (lines 93 to 97: font-accent compiles to the literal family 'Instrument Serif', Georgia, serif), test/unit/tokens-scopes.test.ts (lines 33 to 51: which tokens heritage changes), test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts (all of it: only the fixture page renders ThemeScope, lines 26 to 32; only ThemeScope imports the live file, and lazily, lines 33 to 39; ThemeScope.tsx and themeScopes.ts name no themeHeritage, themeScholastic or features, lines 40 to 45; live.css holds imports only, lines 47 to 80; the font packages are pinned and the lockfile agrees, lines 82 to 91; the dash and tool-name check on the step's files, lines 93 to 115), test/unit/theme-scope.test.tsx (the hoisted mock of live.css at lines 17 to 22 and the heritage cases at lines 46 to 62, 93 to 124 and 143) and test/unit/theme-scope-edges.test.tsx (the freshScope helper at lines 11 to 25 and the heritage rerender at lines 150 to 160), test/unit/geist-mono-glyphs.test.ts (lines 1 to 95: the reader of WOFF2 tables and character maps, the pattern for the glyph pin), test/unit/helpers/cssTokens.ts (read, stripComments and parseRules, for reading CSS in a test), test/unit/test-setup.test.ts (lines 225 to 229: the spec's heritage fonts line), test/unit/redesign-status-step27.test.ts (lines 271 to 272) and test/unit/redesign-status-step29.test.ts (all of it, so the step 30 records leave its expectations true), test/a11y/scope-switch.spec.ts (AC8: switching data-theme on the base fixture moves no box, lines 111 to 198; live.css is fetched only when a live scope renders, lines 201 to 227, which visits /__fixtures/heritage and so will now see a heritage stylesheet there, never a live one), test/a11y/scope-switch-edges.spec.ts, test/a11y/brand-edges.spec.ts (lines 271 to 285: the logo mat read inside a heritage main), test/a11y/tokens.spec.ts, test/a11y/global-setup.ts, test/a11y/baseline.ts and baseline.json (re-read the four that the harness commit changes), so that the flag-off baseline comparison stays green. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and the two notes on the harness, which every step must leave alone): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 30) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. node_modules is installed, but neither font package this slice adds is; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy. Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. Georgia is not installed in this container (fc-list finds no Georgia; the serif faces on this computer are DejaVu Serif, FreeSerif and Liberation Serif), so no browser test here can show the Georgia fallback; see difference 7. Dependencies are exact-pinned (no caret) at versions at least two weeks old (today is 2026-10-21, so published on or before 2026-10-07), with package-lock.json updated by npm install; this slice adds two dependencies (differences 1 and 2). The branch tip is abe7d07 (the harness commit) and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries later commits only once the lead pushes, and the local main ref does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against abe7d07. A full test:a11y run starts servers on ports 8801 and 8802 (after the harness commit each over a database of its own; read global-setup.ts for where), so never run two of them at once, and never run one while a build is running. Build exactly this. The Heritage Club type layer, loaded only inside its scope.

Dependencies, exact-pinned:
- @fontsource/libre-caslon-display: 400, latin, about 24 KB
- @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4: the wght-axis latin file (about 51 KB), not the opsz file at 122 KB

Together they come to about 75 KB, under the 110 KB budget. The italic (about 51 KB) is declared and fetched only when italic text renders.

src/styles/themes/heritage.css, imported lazily by ThemeScope when scope is heritage:
- the font imports
- a Georgia fallback @font-face with size-adjust and ascent-override tuned to keep CLS under 0.1
- --font-display bound to Caslon for h1 and h2 at 32 px and up and display numerals inside the scope, never ratings, scores or tables
- Source Serif body text at 18 px / 1.6 with a 70ch measure in the readers, with lining and tabular figures
- Instrument Serif switched off inside the scope
- a 2 px radius on cards, tables and hero mats only, while controls keep the base radius
- .small-caps: uppercase at 0.85em with 0.07em tracking, because the latin subsets have no smcp or c2sc, so small caps are never synthesised

Inside heritage, Button, Input, chips, StatusBadge, the focus ring, control radius and date and score formats keep base styling. test/unit/heritage-css.test.ts asserts that Instrument Serif is unreachable inside [data-theme=heritage], that Caslon is referenced only by --font-display, and that no control selector is restyled. test/unit/heritage-budget.test.ts sums the woff2 files the scope imports. Nothing renders the heritage scope outside the fixture page until slice 31. Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): Latin subset keeps smcp / c2sc (verify in the brief). (No. GSUB features: the Source Serif 4 latin wght and opsz files have ccmp, dnom, frac, liga, locl, numr, pnum and tnum; Libre Caslon Display latin 400 has dnom, frac, liga and numr. Use the uppercase 0.85em fallback as the brief directs. Re-checked: it holds, read from the 5.3.0 files themselves (fetched with npm pack into a scratch folder and read table by table; nothing is installed in the tree). Libre Caslon Display latin 400: GSUB dnom, frac, liga and numr, GPOS kern, and no smcp, no c2sc, no pnum, no tnum and no lnum. Source Serif 4 latin wght normal, wght italic and opsz normal: GSUB ccmp, dnom, frac, liga, locl, numr, pnum and tnum, GPOS kern, mark and mkmk, and no smcp, no c2sc, no lnum and no onum, so its figures are lining by default (font-variant-numeric: lining-nums would change nothing) and tabular-nums works through tnum. Caslon has no tabular figures, which fits the rule that it sets display numerals and never ratings, scores or tables. All four files (Libre Caslon Display latin 400; Source Serif 4 latin wght normal, wght italic and opsz normal) draw ½ (U+00BD), the en dash (U+2013), the minus sign (U+2212), the digits and the no-break space, and none draws the white circle (U+25CB) or the black circle (U+25CF); see difference 9.) Heritage font budget. (Caslon latin 400: 24,236 bytes. Source Serif 4 latin wght normal: 50,824; italic: 51,516; opsz normal: 122,360. Caslon plus the wght file is about 75 KB. Re-checked: the four sizes hold to the byte, and 24,236 plus 50,824 is 75,060 bytes; but the packages also ship other subsets and the stylesheets declare all of them, so what 'the woff2 files the scope imports' means decides whether the budget holds; see difference 2.) Font package names. (@fontsource/libre-caslon-display and @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4 both resolve at 5.3.0. Re-checked: both names resolve and neither is installed. @fontsource/libre-caslon-display: 5.3.0 is the newest, published Sunday, July 19, 2026 (94 days ago), no dependencies. @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4: 5.3.0 was published Sunday, July 19, 2026 (94 days ago, no dependencies), but the newest, 5.3.1, was published Sunday, October 11, 2026, 10 days ago, which is under two weeks and so is not allowed; pin 5.3.0 for both; see difference 1.) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the tree this slice starts from (slice 29 finished). (1) The packages are not installed, and the newest Source Serif is too new. node_modules/@fontsource holds barlow, barlow-condensed and instrument-serif, and node_modules/@fontsource-variable holds geist and geist-mono; package.json lists the font packages at lines 39 to 43 (Geist with a caret, the rest exact). Both new packages go under dependencies beside them (the browser loads them), exact with no caret, at 5.3.0 each, which the lockfile will hold as two new package entries and two new root lines and nothing else (neither package has a dependency of its own): npm install --save-exact --before=2026-10-07 @fontsource/libre-caslon-display@5.3.0 @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4@5.3.0, through the proxy (npm view and npm pack both answer through it). Check the lockfile diff is only that. If the install fails, say so with the error and stop that part: do not vendor files, loosen the pin or disable TLS checks. Say in the record that @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4 5.3.1 exists (Sunday, October 11, 2026) and why 5.3.0 was chosen. (2) What each package ships, and what 'the woff2 files the scope imports' can mean. Libre Caslon Display 5.3.0 ships latin-400.css (the latin face alone, with no unicode-range), latin-ext-400.css, and 400.css and index.css (identical: both subsets, each with its unicode-range). Its family is 'Libre Caslon Display', and each face names a .woff beside the .woff2, which the bundler emits too: latin 24,236 bytes woff2 (20,048 woff) and latin-ext 16,308 (13,648). Source Serif 4 Variable 5.3.0 has the family 'Source Serif 4 Variable', and index.css is identical to wght.css; wght.css declares six unicode-range faces in roman (cyrillic-ext 18,064 bytes, cyrillic 36,468, greek 20,228, vietnamese 13,448, latin-ext 42,040 and latin 50,824, 181,072 in all), wght-italic.css the same six in italic (18,336, 35,040, 20,536, 13,932, 44,260 and 51,516), and opsz.css, opsz-italic.css, standard.css and standard-italic.css the larger optical-size files (latin opsz normal 122,360, italic 130,188), which the manifest rules out. There is no stylesheet for one subset of the variable package. Its package exports './files/*.woff2', so a file can be named by path. Latin covers U+0000 to U+00FF and U+2000 to U+206F, so it holds ½, the en dash and the minus sign. The browser fetches only a face whose unicode-range the text uses (the Barlow imports of live.css show the bundler side: the a11y build holds every subset of every weight beside live-m7TjVD57.css, 8,313 bytes, 42 font files in all, yet a visitor fetches the latin ones). So the budget depends on how heritage.css reaches the files: the latin pair is 75,060 bytes; Caslon's two subsets with the six roman faces would be 40,544 plus 181,072, 221,616 bytes, which fails 110 KB if every declared file counts. The spec says 'Budget ≤ 110 KB woff2, latin subset' (line 295). Pick one and record it as a judgement call: either heritage.css names only the two latin files (Caslon through latin-400.css; Source Serif through a face of its own that names the package's latin file by path, which the bundler must be seen to resolve and emit), or it imports the packages' stylesheets whole and test/unit/heritage-budget.test.ts sums the files whose unicode-range covers U+0020 to U+007E, which are the files the browser fetches for English text. Either way the test reads the real stylesheets, the real ranges and the real file sizes (no constants copied from this brief), sums the normal faces only, holds the sum to 110,000 bytes (so either reading of 110 KB passes), and fails on a planted extra file or a planted subset; the italic is declared (a face with font-style italic, from its own stylesheet or face) and left out of the sum, and the test shows the italic file is named only by an italic face, so it is fetched only when italic text renders. Report the sum. (3) No font token exists for heritage today. src/index.css's heritage blocks (lines 599 to 630) hold grounds, ink, rules and gold-ink only. There is no --font-display anywhere in src, tests or scripts, no heritage font-family and no font-heading use. font-accent is declared in @theme inline as 'Instrument Serif', Georgia, serif (line 47) and the utility compiles to that literal family (token-utilities.test.ts line 96; the built stylesheet holds both a --font-accent variable and .font-accent with the family written out), so re-pointing --font-accent inside the scope would change nothing for a class that reads the literal: to switch Instrument Serif off inside the scope, heritage.css must override the .font-accent rule itself for descendants of [data-theme="heritage"] (and --font-accent for anything that reads it), and heritage-css.test.ts must prove unreachability from the rules (no rule that applies inside the scope resolves a font-family naming Instrument Serif), not from the token alone. No page or component uses font-accent today (a search of src finds only index.css). Instrument Serif's @import stays in src/index.css (tokens.test.ts pins it), so its face is declared on every page and a file is fetched only when text uses it. --font-display is new: define it only in heritage.css, bound to Caslon with the fallback face and the serif stack behind it, so 'Caslon is referenced only by --font-display' can be tested; name the fallback faces so the test can tell a face declaration from a use. (4) The hooks the manifest names do not exist. Card (src/components/ui/card.tsx) and Table (src/components/ui/table.tsx) carry no data-slot, Input and the other form fields carry none (Button, the status tags and the chips do), no 'reader' exists (the bylaws and minutes reader is WS14's) and the one 'mat' in the tree is data-slot="lca-logo-mat" on /about (AboutPage.tsx line 17). The 2px radius on cards, tables and hero mats, and the 18px / 1.6 / 70ch measure in the readers, therefore need hooks that heritage.css names: a small documented set of classes or data attributes that the heritage layout (step 31) and the readers (WS14) will put on their own elements, plus data-slot="lca-logo-mat", which exists. Do not edit card.tsx or table.tsx (every page uses them; neither is on the manifest's list); if you find you must, record it under Files beyond the step's list with every pin it moves. Controls keep the base radius, and no font or radius rule may reach a control: a button, input, select, textarea, [data-slot="button"], [data-slot="status-badge"], a chip or the focus ring. Because buttons and inputs inherit their font, heritage.css must set font-family on named hooks only (h1, h2, the reader hook, .small-caps) and never on the scope container, so a form drawn inside a base scope inside heritage keeps its Geist. Make heritage-css.test.ts read the real selectors and fail when a control selector is restyled, on planted cases, with the names put together when the test runs. (5) 'h1 and h2 at 32 px and up' cannot be a selector: CSS cannot test a rendered size. Pages today draw h1 as text-3xl (30 px) below the sm breakpoint and sm:text-4xl (36 px) above it (PageHero.tsx lines 95 and 99; the fixture's h1 is text-3xl) and h2 as text-xl (20 px). Decide how the rule honours the floor, and record it as a judgement call: for instance a media query at the width where h1 reaches 36 px, with h2 bound to Caslon only through a hook class that carries its own size, or a floor set on the hook; do not let Caslon reach a heading under 32 px, and do not set a font-size on h1 or h2 that overrides the pages' own utilities. Rules in heritage.css are unlayered and so beat the stylesheet's utility layer whatever the specificity: say which layer you write in and why. Display numerals (a class, for the figures such as '1915' and '300+') never reach a rating, a score or a table cell; the Geist Mono rule for every number, ½ and notation in every scope is not touched. (6) Heritage tokens apply only under newLook, and heritage.css loads whether or not newLook is on. ThemeScope must name no flag (theme-scope-wiring.test.ts lines 40 to 45 fail on themeHeritage, themeScholastic or features in ThemeScope.tsx and themeScopes.ts), so it imports heritage.css whenever a heritage scope renders, on either build; the colours already wait for :root[data-look="new"] (The scope switches need newLook, line 893). Every rule in heritage.css that sets a font, a size, a radius or a measure is therefore written under :root[data-look="new"] [data-theme="heritage"] (the same selector shape the colour block uses), so a heritage scope with newLook off looks as it does today. Only the @font-face declarations and the fallback faces may sit outside that guard. (7) The Georgia fallback cannot be seen here, so it is computed. Measured from the 5.3.0 files: Libre Caslon Display latin 400 has 1000 units per em, hhea ascent 970, descent 266, line gap 0, OS/2 xAvgCharWidth 494, x-height 424, cap height 690, and typographic metrics in use; Source Serif 4 latin wght normal has 1000 units per em, hhea ascent 1036, descent 335, line gap 0, xAvgCharWidth 513 (510 in the italic, 558 in opsz normal), x-height 475, cap height 670. Georgia's own metrics are not in the tree or the container: take them from a published source or a font that carries them, write the source and the arithmetic into heritage.css's header and the record, and declare the fallback faces (src: local('Georgia'), with size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override) one for each face, named so the test can tell them from the real faces, with the font stack Caslon, its fallback, Georgia, serif and Source Serif, its fallback, Georgia, serif. After the build, open the emitted heritage stylesheet and confirm size-adjust, ascent-override, descent-override and line-gap-override survived the stylesheet build; if one did not, say so and work around it in the source. The manifest's risk stands: the overrides are tuned against the real fonts here and CLS is measured in step 31 once the layout applies the scope (AC11); record that, and do not claim a CLS figure this slice cannot measure. (8) Step 30 has no acceptance row. AC11 (line 35, 'Heritage fonts stay off /; no layout shift from the font swap'), AC12 (line 36) and AC13 (line 37) are all step 31's, and the manifest's 'AC/K row' has no row to fill. Add one sentence to each of the AC11 and AC12 rows, keeping their first three cells and their word 'Planned:' at the start of the fourth, in the pattern of AC12's 'Step 22 lays the first half:': AC11's says the heritage font file is a lazy chunk that only ThemeScope imports (the first half of the row, the file kept off /, in step 30 and its network-log proof in step 31), and replaces its existing clause 'the heritage font chunk is step 30' so the row does not contradict itself; AC12's says test/unit/heritage-css.test.ts holds the Instrument Serif and Caslon rules of the spec's line 359 (Instrument Serif unreachable inside the scope, Caslon bound only to --font-display for h1 and h2). Leave AC13 and AC8 as they are. No test pins these two rows today (a search of test/unit finds none); the step 30 record test will. (9) The glyph pin the manifest does not list. Follow-up line 1600 ('The heritage faces' glyphs (step 27)') says step 30 pins that each latin file has ½ and that neither has the white and black circles, as test/unit/geist-mono-glyphs.test.ts does for Geist Mono, the face chess data is drawn in. Add test/unit/heritage-glyphs.test.ts for it (reusing that file's table and character-map reader by copying the function, not by importing a test file; the shape of a shared helper is yours to choose, and a new helper under test/unit/helpers is fine) over the installed Caslon latin and Source Serif latin wght files, normal and italic: ½, the en dash, the minus sign, the digits and the no-break space present; U+25CB and U+25CF absent; and the file whose unicode-range covers U+00BD is the latin one. Already measured: all present, both circles absent, in every file listed. The follow-up then gets Done in step 30. (10) A production build will not carry the heritage chunk; only the browser-test builds will. ThemeScope renders only on the fixture page (ScopeFixturePage.tsx, routed in the a11y mode only), so the production dist holds no ThemeScope, no live stylesheet and no Barlow file, and will hold no heritage stylesheet or Caslon or Source Serif file after this slice: the production dist (npm run build) must come out byte for byte as at step 29, 133 files, CSS 127,896 bytes in one file, JavaScript 2,586,164 bytes in 104 files; report it before and after and explain any change. The 'separate lazy chunk' check is made on the a11y builds that npm run test:a11y writes (dist-a11y-on and dist-a11y-off): there live.css is live-m7TjVD57.css (8,313 bytes, with its font files beside it) and is named only by the ScopeFixturePage chunk, and heritage.css must come out the same way, as its own heritage-<hash>.css named only by that chunk and by nothing on the home page's path; list those files with their sizes in the record, and show that index-*.css and the main chunk do not name the heritage faces. No new browser spec is on the manifest's list, so do not add one; AC11's network-log and layout-shift proofs are step 31's (note them in the record).
